questions.stem: What is 7 squared?
questions.explanation: Squaring means multiplying a number by itself: 7 × 7 = 49. Doubling gives 14, which is the usual slip.
questions.teaching:
Squaring a number means multiplying it by itself, and the name comes from geometry: a square with sides of that length has that many unit squares in it.

So the calculation is the number times the number, not the number times two — that is doubling, and it is the classic confusion. Written with a small raised 2, the index counts how many copies are multiplied. Knowing the squares up to about 15 by heart is worth the effort, because they turn up constantly in Pythagoras problems, area calculations and quadratic work.

questions.stem: What is the square root of 64?
questions.explanation: 8 × 8 = 64. Halving 64 gives 32, which is a different operation.
questions.teaching:
A square root asks the reverse question of squaring: what number, multiplied by itself, produces this?

So work forwards through squares you know rather than trying to work backwards. Six times six is 36, seven times seven is 49, eight times eight is 64, nine times nine is 81 — run through them until one lands on the target. Halving is the tempting shortcut and it is wrong. Knowing the squares up to 15 makes this immediate, and it also tells you when a root will not come out exactly.

questions.stem: Which of these is a prime number?
questions.explanation: 13 has exactly two factors, 1 and itself. 15 = 3 × 5, 21 = 3 × 7 and 9 = 3 × 3.
questions.teaching:
A prime number has exactly two factors: one and itself. That definition does the work if you apply it carefully.

Test a candidate by trying to divide it by 2, 3, 5, 7 and so on — if anything other than one and the number itself divides evenly, it is not prime. Two edge cases catch people: 1 has only one factor so it does not qualify, and 2 is prime despite being even, since being even only means divisible by 2, which is itself. Every other even number fails.

questions.stem: What is -5 + 8?
questions.explanation: Starting at -5 and moving 8 in the positive direction lands on 3.
questions.teaching:
Adding and subtracting negative numbers is easiest on a number line, where the operation tells you which way to move.

Start at the first number. Adding moves you right; subtracting moves you left. A negative number after the operation reverses that direction — so subtracting a negative moves you right, which is why two minus signs together behave like a plus. Work out the direction first and the distance second, and read off where you land. The commonest error is guessing the sign of the answer rather than tracking the movement, so a rough sketch of the line is worth the few seconds it takes.

questions.stem: What is -6 - 4?
questions.explanation: Subtracting moves further in the negative direction, so -6 - 4 = -10.
questions.teaching:
Adding and subtracting negative numbers is easiest on a number line, where the operation tells you which way to move.

Start at the first number. Adding moves you right; subtracting moves you left. A negative number after the operation reverses that direction — so subtracting a negative moves you right, which is why two minus signs together behave like a plus. Work out the direction first and the distance second, and read off where you land. The commonest error is guessing the sign of the answer rather than tracking the movement, so a rough sketch of the line is worth the few seconds it takes.

questions.stem: What is 0.25 as a fraction in simplest form?
questions.explanation: 0.25 is 25 hundredths, which simplifies to 1/4.
questions.teaching:
Converting a decimal to a fraction starts from what the decimal places mean.

The first place is tenths, the second hundredths, the third thousandths. So a two-place decimal is that many hundredths, which gives the fraction immediately. Then simplify by dividing top and bottom by their highest common factor — that step is where marks are usually lost, since an unsimplified answer is often not accepted. Check by dividing your fraction back out and confirming you recover the original decimal.

questions.stem: What is 3/4 as a decimal?
questions.explanation: 3 divided by 4 gives 0.75. Reading the digits as 0.34 mixes up the numerator and denominator.
questions.teaching:
A fraction is a division waiting to happen: the line between the numbers means divide the top by the bottom.

So converting means carrying out that division. For fractions with denominators of 2, 4, 5, 8, 10 or 100 the result terminates neatly, and those are worth knowing by heart because they come up constantly. Denominators like 3, 6, 7 and 9 give recurring decimals instead. A useful check: a fraction smaller than one must give a decimal below 1, so if your answer exceeds that you have divided the wrong way round.

questions.stem: What is 50% of 80?
questions.explanation: 50 per cent is one half, so halve the amount: 80 becomes 40. Multiplying by 50 rather than by 0.5 is the usual slip.
questions.teaching:
Percentages are fractions with a denominator of 100, so 'per cent' literally means 'per hundred'.

Finding a percentage of an amount means converting to a fraction or decimal and multiplying. The common ones are worth knowing as fractions: 50% is a half, 25% is a quarter, 10% is a tenth, and 1% is a hundredth. Building other percentages from these is faster than any formula — 15% is 10% plus half of 10%, and 35% is 25% plus 10%. It also gives you a sense of whether an answer is plausible.

questions.stem: What is 10% of 250?
questions.explanation: 10% is one tenth, so divide by 10.
questions.teaching:
Ten per cent is a tenth, and finding a tenth of any number is simply moving the decimal point one place to the left.

That single trick is the foundation of most mental percentage work. One per cent moves the point two places. From those two you can build almost anything: 20% is double the tenth, 5% is half of it, 15% is the tenth plus half the tenth. Doing it this way is faster than reaching for a calculator and, more usefully, tells you immediately whether a calculator answer is the right size.

questions.stem: Which number is largest?
questions.explanation: Compare place by place: 0.7 is seven tenths, far larger than seven hundredths.

questions.stem: What is 3.6 rounded to the nearest whole number?
questions.explanation: The digit after the decimal point is 6, which is 5 or more, so round up.
questions.teaching:
Rounding replaces a number with a nearby simpler one, and the rule depends on the digit immediately after the place you are rounding to.

Look at that next digit only — not the whole tail. If it is 5 or more, round up; if it is 4 or less, round down. Digits beyond it do not matter, which is the point people most often get wrong by rounding repeatedly from the right. Rounding is what makes estimates possible, and estimating before a calculation is the cheapest way to catch a slip.

questions.stem: What is 1/2 + 1/4?
questions.explanation: Rewrite 1/2 as 2/4, then 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4. Adding numerators and denominators separately is the classic error.
questions.teaching:
Fractions can only be added when the pieces are the same size, which means the denominators must match first.

Find a common denominator, convert each fraction by multiplying top and bottom by the same number — which changes how it looks without changing its value — and only then add the numerators, leaving the denominator alone. Adding the denominators together is the classic error. A sanity check catches it every time: the answer must be bigger than either fraction you started with.

questions.stem: In the ratio 2 : 3, if there are 4 of the first quantity, how many of the second?
questions.explanation: The ratio doubles from 2 to 4, so the second part doubles from 3 to 6.

questions.stem: What is 12 written as a product of prime factors?
questions.explanation: Prime factorisation uses only primes. 2 × 6 and 3 × 4 both contain composite numbers.

questions.stem: What is the value of 4 × (3 + 2)?
questions.explanation: Brackets first: 3 + 2 = 5, then 4 × 5 = 20. Ignoring the brackets gives 14.

questions.stem: Which fraction is equivalent to 2/3?
questions.explanation: Multiplying top and bottom by 2 gives 4/6. 6/3 is the reciprocal-style flip and equals 2.

questions.stem: What is 0.5 × 0.5?
questions.explanation: Half of a half is a quarter. Multiplying by a number less than 1 makes the result smaller.

questions.stem: What is -3 × 4?
questions.explanation: A negative multiplied by a positive gives a negative result.
questions.teaching:
Multiplying and dividing with negatives follows one short sign rule, and the arithmetic is otherwise ordinary.

Do the multiplication or division as though both numbers were positive, then decide the sign separately: if the two signs are the same, the result is positive; if they differ, it is negative. A useful way to see why is that multiplying by a negative flips direction on the number line, so flipping twice puts you back where you started. Note this rule is for multiplying and dividing only — adding and subtracting negatives works quite differently.

questions.stem: What is -12 ÷ -3?
questions.explanation: A negative divided by a negative gives a positive result.
questions.teaching:
Multiplying and dividing with negatives follows one short sign rule, and the arithmetic is otherwise ordinary.

questions.stem: A jacket costs $80 and is reduced by 25%. What is the sale price?
questions.explanation: 25% of 80 is 20, so the price falls to 60. Answering 20 gives the discount rather than the price.

questions.stem: What is 15 as a percentage of 60?
questions.explanation: 15 out of 60 simplifies to 1/4, and 1/4 expressed as a percentage is 25%.

questions.stem: Which is the better buy: 500 g for $4.00 or 750 g for $5.40?
options: They cost the same per kilogram
questions.explanation: 500 g for $4.00 is $8.00 per kg; 750 g for $5.40 is $7.20 per kg. Comparing unit price is the standard 'best buy' method.

questions.stem: What is 2/3 × 3/4?
questions.explanation: Multiply across: 6/12, which simplifies to 1/2.

questions.stem: What is 3/4 ÷ 1/2?
questions.explanation: Dividing by a fraction means multiplying by its reciprocal: 3/4 × 2/1 = 6/4 = 1 1/2. Note the answer is larger than the original.

questions.stem: Estimate 197 × 4 by rounding first.
questions.explanation: 197 rounds to 200, and 200 × 4 = 800. The exact answer, 788, is close to the estimate.

questions.stem: Which list is in order from smallest to largest?
questions.explanation: On a number line, more negative means smaller, so -5 is the smallest.

questions.stem: What is 8% of 250?
Write 5 400 000 in expanded notation using powers of 10.
questions.explanation: Expanded notation writes each digit against its own power of ten and adds the parts. 5.4 × 10^6 is scientific notation — the same value written a different way, and a separate idea.

questions.stem: A jumper is $60 after a 20% discount. What was the original price?
questions.explanation: $60 represents 80% of the original, so one per cent is $0.75 and the original is $75. Adding 20% to $60 gives $72, which is the common trap.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT equivalent to 0.4?
questions.explanation: 4/100 is 0.04. The other three are all four tenths.

questions.stem: What is the value of 5 + 3 × 2?
questions.explanation: Multiplication is done before addition: 3 × 2 = 6, then 5 + 6 = 11. Working left to right gives 16.

questions.stem: A shop raises a price by 10%, then reduces the new price by 10%. What is the overall effect?
options: The final price is slightly less than the original
The final price equals the original
The final price is slightly more than the original
questions.explanation: The reduction applies to a larger amount than the increase did. $100 becomes $110, then $99 — a 1% fall overall.

questions.stem: Which statement about square roots is correct?
options: The square root of a number between 0 and 1 is larger than the number itself
The square root of a number is always smaller than the number
Square roots only exist for even numbers
questions.explanation: The square root of 0.25 is 0.5, which is larger. The 'always smaller' rule only holds for numbers above 1.

questions.stem: Why is estimation useful even when a calculator is available?
options: It checks whether the calculated answer is reasonable and catches keying errors
It is always more accurate than a calculator
It replaces the need to calculate
questions.explanation: Estimation is a check on plausibility. A mistyped digit produces an answer that an estimate immediately flags as wrong.

questions.stem: A recipe for 4 people uses 300 g of rice. How much is needed for 10 people?
questions.explanation: 300 ÷ 4 = 75 g per person, and 75 × 10 = 750 g.

questions.stem: Which number has exactly three factors?
questions.explanation: The square of a prime has exactly three factors: 1, the prime, and the square. 49 gives 1, 7 and 49.

questions.stem: Two numbers are in the ratio 3 : 5 and add to 64. What is the larger number?
questions.explanation: There are 8 parts in total, so each part is 8. The larger is 5 × 8 = 40.

questions.stem: What is 2^3 × 2^4?
questions.explanation: Multiplying powers of the same base adds the indices: 3 + 4 = 7. Multiplying the indices gives the common wrong answer.

questions.stem: Why does rounding 2.45 to one decimal place give a different answer to rounding 2.449?
options: 2.45 rounds up to 2.5 while 2.449 rounds down to 2.4
questions.explanation: Rounding depends on the digit immediately after the place being kept: 5 rounds up, 4 rounds down.

questions.stem: A price of $45 includes 10% GST. What was the price before GST?
questions.explanation: $45 is 110% of the pre-GST price, so divide by 1.1. Subtracting 10% of $45 gives $40.50, which is the common error.

questions.stem: What is 9 squared?

questions.stem: What is the square root of 100?
questions.explanation: Ten times ten is one hundred. Halving gives 50, a different operation.

questions.stem: What is 1/2 as a percentage?
questions.explanation: One half is fifty hundredths, so 50 per cent.

questions.stem: What is 0.1 as a fraction?
questions.explanation: One tenth. Two decimal places would give hundredths.

questions.explanation: A positive times a negative gives a negative product.

questions.stem: Which of these is a composite number?
questions.explanation: Nine has factors 1, 3 and 9. The others are prime.

questions.stem: What is 25% of 40?
questions.explanation: 25 per cent is one quarter, and a quarter of 40 is 10.

questions.stem: What is 7.48 rounded to one decimal place?
questions.explanation: The second decimal digit is 8, so the first rounds up.

questions.stem: What is 2/5 of 60?
questions.explanation: One fifth of 60 is 12, so two fifths is 24.

questions.stem: A $45 item has 20% added. What is the new price?
questions.explanation: 20% of 45 is 9, so the price rises to 54. Answering 9 gives the increase only.

questions.stem: Which is larger: 3/5 or 0.65?
questions.explanation: 3/5 is 0.6, which is smaller than 0.65. Converting to a common form makes the comparison straightforward.

questions.stem: Simplify the ratio 12 : 18.
questions.explanation: Divide both parts by the highest common factor, 6.

questions.stem: What is the highest common factor of 24 and 36?
questions.explanation: 12 divides both, and nothing larger does. 72 is the lowest common multiple.

questions.stem: What is the lowest common multiple of 4 and 6?
questions.explanation: 12 is the smallest number both divide into. 24 is a common multiple but not the lowest.

questions.stem: A 300 g pack costs $2.40. What is the price per 100 g?
questions.explanation: Divide by 3 to get the price per 100 g.

questions.stem: What is 1/3 + 1/6?
The temperature rises from -3 °C by 8 degrees. What is the new temperature?
questions.explanation: Counting up from -3 by 8 passes through zero and reaches 5.

questions.stem: What is 0.6 × 30?
questions.explanation: 0.6 is six tenths, and six tenths of 30 is 18.

questions.stem: A number is increased by 50%, then decreased by 50%. What fraction of the original remains?
questions.explanation: 100 becomes 150, then loses 75 to give 75 — three quarters of the original.

questions.stem: Which is the best estimate for 48 × 21?
questions.explanation: Rounding to 50 × 20 gives 1000, close to the exact 1008.

questions.stem: A jacket is discounted 30% to $84. What was the original price?
questions.explanation: $84 is 70% of the original, so divide by 0.7. Adding 30% to $84 gives $109.20, the common trap.

questions.stem: What is 5^3?
questions.explanation: Five multiplied by itself three times: 5 × 5 × 5.

questions.stem: Two numbers are in the ratio 2 : 7 and differ by 25. What is the smaller?
questions.explanation: The difference is 5 parts, so each part is 5, making the smaller 2 × 5 = 10.

questions.stem: Why is 0.999... often said to equal 1?
options: The difference between them is smaller than any positive number, so they are the same value
It is an approximation that rounds to 1
questions.explanation: This is a genuine result rather than a rounding convention, and it surprises most people the first time.

questions.stem: A recipe scaled by 3/4 uses 450 g of flour. How much did the original use?
questions.explanation: 450 is three quarters of the original, so divide by 3 and multiply by 4.

questions.stem: Which statement about prime numbers is correct?
options: 2 is the only even prime number
questions.explanation: Every other even number has 2 as a factor. 1 has only one factor so is not prime, and 9 is odd but composite.

questions.stem: What is the value of 10^0?
questions.explanation: Any non-zero number raised to the power zero equals 1, which follows from the index laws.

questions.stem: Estimate 7.9 × 4.1 without calculating exactly.
questions.explanation: Rounding to 8 × 4 gives 32, close to the exact 32.39.

questions.stem: What is 4 cubed?
questions.explanation: Four multiplied by itself three times: 4 × 4 × 4 = 64.
questions.teaching:
An index tells you how many copies of the base to multiply together, not what to multiply the base by.

So a number raised to the third power means three of them multiplied in a row: work through it in steps rather than in one go, since doing the first multiplication and then multiplying the result again is far less error-prone. Squaring means two copies, cubing means three. The classic mistake is multiplying the base by the index, which gives a much smaller answer — check by asking whether your result looks big enough.

questions.explanation: Nine times nine is eighty-one. Halving gives 40.5, a different operation.

questions.stem: What is 3/5 as a decimal?
questions.explanation: Three divided by five gives 0.6.

questions.stem: What is 75% as a fraction in simplest form?
questions.explanation: 75 hundredths simplifies to three quarters.

questions.explanation: Five divides evenly into twenty. Thirty is a multiple, not a factor.

questions.stem: What is 100% of 63?
questions.explanation: One hundred per cent is the whole amount, unchanged.

questions.explanation: The third decimal digit is 7, so the second rounds up.

questions.explanation: Dividing top and bottom by 2 gives one half.

questions.explanation: Ten per cent is 35, so forty per cent is 4 × 35 = 140.

questions.stem: A price falls from $80 to $60. What is the percentage decrease?
questions.explanation: The fall of $20 is compared with the original $80, giving one quarter.

questions.stem: What is 5/6 - 1/3?

questions.explanation: 2 kg is $4.50 per kg and 5 kg is $4.20 per kg.

questions.explanation: There are 12 parts, so each is 5, and the largest share is 5 × 5 = 25.

questions.stem: What is 1.5 × 0.4?
questions.explanation: One and a half lots of 0.4 gives 0.6.

questions.explanation: Rounding to 300 ÷ 5 gives 60, close to the exact 61.6.

questions.stem: Which is greater: 2^10 or 10^2?
questions.explanation: Repeated doubling grows far faster than squaring a larger base once.

questions.stem: A quantity increases by 10% each year for two years. What is the total increase?
questions.explanation: 100 becomes 110, then 121 — the second increase applies to the larger amount.

questions.stem: Why is dividing by a fraction less than 1 giving a larger answer?
options: You are asking how many small parts fit into the amount, which is many
questions.explanation: 6 divided by 1/2 asks how many halves are in 6, which is 12.

questions.stem: A shop offers '30% off, then a further 10% off'. What single discount is equivalent?
questions.explanation: The second discount applies to 70% of the original, giving 63% remaining and therefore 37% off.

questions.stem: What is the highest common factor of 45 and 60?
questions.explanation: Fifteen divides both and nothing larger does. 180 is the lowest common multiple.

questions.stem: Why does rounding early in a multi-step calculation cause error?
options: Rounding changes the order in which steps must be done
Each rounding introduces a small error that compounds through later steps
Rounding is only a problem when dividing
Rounding errors cancel out if you round up and down alternately
questions.explanation: Rounding only at the final step keeps the accumulated error smallest.

questions.stem: A number multiplied by itself gives 0.36. What is the number?
questions.explanation: 0.6 × 0.6 = 0.36. Note the square root of a number below 1 is larger than the number.

questions.stem: What is 60% of 40?
questions.explanation: A percentage is a fraction out of 100, so 60% of 40 is 60/100 x 40 = 24. The quickest route is usually 1% first: 1% of 40 is 0.4, and 60 lots of that is 24. The common slip is dropping the division by 100 and working out 60 x 40 = 2400. Any percentage below 100 has to give you less than you started with, so an answer larger than 40 is wrong before you check anything else.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to evaluate  4 + 3 x (6 - 3)²
questions.explanation: Brackets always come first, so 6 - 3 = 3 before anything else happens. Indices are next, giving 3² = 9, then multiplication, then addition last — the order the acronym BIDMAS records. Working strictly left to right instead would give a different answer, because addition would happen before the multiplication it is supposed to follow.
